findings.condition: bookingSummary() derives canReturn/canCheckout from `p.permissions.includes('RENTAL_RETURN'|'RENTAL_CHECKOUT')`, which is a global (non-store-scoped) permission list on StaffPrincipal. Store-scope safety for these two flags is not independently re-checked in this method; it depends entirely on the single earlier `this.authorize('BOOKING_VIEW',[receivingStore])` call having already confirmed `receivingStore ∈ p.storeIds`, and on the same `p` object/storeIds being reused unchanged for the rest of the function.
findings.impact: Not currently exploitable (the call order is correct today, and the returned p.storeIds cannot change mid-function), but the store-scope guarantee for canReturn/canCheckout is not locally self-evident within bookingSummary the way it is in the sibling method returnWorkspace, which explicitly calls `this.authorize('RENTAL_RETURN',[receivingStore])` a second time. A future refactor that reorders these calls, caches/reuses a principal from elsewhere, or removes the BOOKING_VIEW store-scope check would silently regress cross-store authorization without any local assertion catching it.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/wear/service.ts: bookingSummary (lines ~33-42) contrasts with returnWorkspace (lines ~43-51), where the latter calls `await this.authorize('BOOKING_VIEW',[receivingStore]);await this.authorize('RENTAL_RETURN',[receivingStore]);` explicitly before reading unresolved/batches, while bookingSummary only calls authorize('BOOKING_VIEW',[receivingStore]) once and then inspects p.permissions directly for RENTAL_RETURN/RENTAL_CHECKOUT without a second scoped authorize call.
findings.fix: Add an explicit scoped check in bookingSummary mirroring returnWorkspace's pattern, e.g. compute canReturn/canCheckout via a store-scoped authorize-style helper (or assert `receivingStore` is in `p.storeIds` locally before setting canReturn/canCheckout), so the invariant is verifiable within the function itself rather than relying on an earlier call's side effect.
findings.test: Add a unit/integration test constructing a StaffPrincipal with global RENTAL_RETURN permission but storeIds limited to ONSEN_BASE only, call bookingSummary(bookingId, 'MOUNTAIN_BASE') and assert it throws FORBIDDEN (currently true only because the first authorize('BOOKING_VIEW',['MOUNTAIN_BASE']) call fails); additionally add a white-box test/lint rule that fails if bookingSummary's canReturn/canCheckout computation is ever reached without a preceding store-scoped authorize call covering the exact permission being read.
